name: ZeroQuant-V2 (systematic PTQ study + low-rank compensation LoRC)
bits: study spans w4a16 and w4a8; also covers weight-only and activation-only variants across 125M-176B models
activation_scheme: None introduced. The paper's own conclusion is that activation quantization is the weak point: 'none of the current methods can achieve the original model quality for quantization with either INT4-weight or INT4-weight-and-INT8-activation'. Its contribution is Low-Rank Compensation (LoRC), which adds low-rank matrices to recover model quality after quantization at minimal size increase.
quality_delta: No single number in the abstract. The finding itself is the result: activation quantization is more susceptible to damage than weight quantization, and smaller models often tolerate activation quantization better than larger ones.
notes: Enum mismatch: 'gptq' is the closest enum because ZeroQuant-V2 is a weight-only PTQ method in the GPTQ lineage (it evaluates and extends RTN, GPTQ and ZeroQuant rather than introducing a new grid format). Request the parent add 'zeroquant'. Two things a reader should not get wrong: (1) this is ZeroQuant V2, distinct from the v1 record; v1's headline is INT8 weight+activation with layer-by-layer distillation for BERT and GPT-3 style models, v1 has no separate record here and would need one added; (2) the 'group-wise 3-bit' claim sometimes attributed to ZeroQuant-V2 is NOT supported by the abstract - the abstract mentions no 3-bit configuration at all. Do not record 3-bit for this method without reading the experiments section. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (parent agent, 2026-10-03): scheme was 'gptq' (a proxy recorded while the enum lacked a legal value) and is now 'zeroquant'.
